races.name: Celebrate National Racehorse Week 2026 Mares' Maiden Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Diamond Grace
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has placed twice at 2m on good ground; Jonjo O'Neill Jr. in the saddle for a yard running at 2/16 over 14 days, 41 days since last run is fine, and uncontested lead on fast ground suits her perfectly.

runners_data.name: Dreaming Of The Dr
runners_data.note: Three runs have yielded no win or place finish and she shapes as a complete unknown stylistically; Luke Scott (3) riding for a stable at 0/7 over 14 days gives little confidence, and good ground hasn't helped her previously.

runners_data.name: La Bamba Chica
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning after 130 days — fitness is the main question — but her one run on good ground produced a fifth, and Richie McLernon can put her handy from the front to capitalise on any leader weakness.

runners_data.name: Letmeseethecolts
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with genuine placed form on good ground and the best winning strike-rate in the field at 1W from 15 similar-ground runs; Nathan Moscrop will need the pace to be brisk enough to reel in a controlled Diamond Grace.

runners_data.name: Pretty Spontaneous
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and going preference unknown, with a jumping error and a fall on her record making trust a concern especially over hurdles on fast ground; Chad Bament (5) taking the ride adds to the uncertainty and 100 days off magnifies the risk.

runners_data.name: Guts And Glory
runners_data.note: Two seconds on soft ground suggest she handles a soft surface better than today's good-to-firm, which is an unresolved question; Stan Sheppard keeps her prominent and she's fresh enough at 136 days, but the going is a query.

runners_data.name: Princess Of Ballea
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who has run six times on good or good-firm and has yet to win; Harry Reed takes the ride but five of her six career efforts show she fades rather than finishes, and the step back to 2m2½f from 2m3f doesn't obviously help.

runners_data.name: Steal A Glance
runners_data.note: Prominent-running mare for Anthony Honeyball who has finished no better than third in five runs on good ground; Sam Twiston-Davies gives her the best jockey in the race but a form string of 73-955 offers scant encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Diamond Grace is the sole confirmed front-runner and looks set to stride into an uncontested lead from the outset, dictating a sustainable gallop over 2m2½f on good-to-firm ground at Stratford. La Bamba Chica and Guts And Glory will push forward prominently but neither has the profile to seriously challenge for the lead, meaning Diamond Grace can control tempo entirely on her own terms. The pace should be honest but measured, with the field likely strung out in orderly fashion behind a relaxed leader. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-leading types who travel within striking range without expending energy chasing, and with no pressure expected up front, horses forced to make ground from midfield or further back face a stiff task if Diamond Grace is allowed to coast at the right tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Diamond Grace Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Grace dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and nothing goes forward to press her.
scenarios.body: Diamond Grace settles into an unhurried rhythm, jumps clean in front and simply lengthens from the last to hold off challengers; Jonjo O'Neill Jr. gets a dream lead on a mare who has shown she handles good ground over similar trips.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Grace ties herself up or makes a jumping error and La Bamba Chica or Guts And Glory use their proximity to pounce.
scenarios.body: La Bamba Chica, returning from 130 days off but with one run on similar ground suggesting she handles it, and Guts And Glory, who has placed twice at this trip on soft, are both close enough to react immediately to any Diamond Grace falter.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely strong enough to soften up the leaders and Letmeseethecolts or Princess Of Ballea can pick off tiring rivals.
scenarios.body: Letmeseethecolts has placed four times from midfield on good ground and Moscrop can time a late run if the pace proves stronger than expected; Princess Of Ballea has finishing form at slightly shorter trips but good ground has caught her out before.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the unexposed or lightly-raced mares — Pretty Spontaneous or Dreaming Of The Dr — produce a career-best under positive handling.
scenarios.body: Pretty Spontaneous remains an unknown quantity given a career plagued by jumping errors and a long absence, while Dreaming Of The Dr has shown zero form in three starts but the low-grade field leaves room for a bounce; either would need a significant improvement to feature.

watchPoints.text: Diamond Grace — if she flukes a clean round and settles sweetly for Jonjo O'Neill Jr., her uncontested lead could prove devastating and she warrants close scrutiny from the first hurdle onward.
La Bamba Chica — at 130 days off with only one hurdles run on her card, fitness is unproven; watch how sharply she travels in the opening mile as a guide to whether she's ready to compete.
Pretty Spontaneous — her record of falls and jumping errors (hg:t suggests a tongue-tie is being used) makes her a race-safety concern on a fast surface; watch at every flight.
Guts And Glory — her placed form came entirely on soft, so monitor how she moves on the good-to-firm in the early stages as any sign of discomfort would quickly relegate her from any scenario.
Letmeseethecolts — pace scenario dependent; if Diamond Grace crawls, Moscrop has nothing to peg back and his hold-up position becomes a liability rather than an asset.

races.name: Stratford Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Bells Of Ufford
runners_data.note: Solid each-way form at 20f on good ground (P54-25) and Tim Vaughan's runners carry decent sim-going stats here; a natural hold-up horse who will race at the rear, making any run dependent on a well-run race that generates something to close into.|

runners_data.name: Brionywells
runners_data.note: Two recent wins at 23f on good ground make the trip and going profile highly relevant, and Nick Slatter claims 3lb; a hold-up type by design, but at 8/11 sim-going and with strong recent form, Brionywells is the most credentialled closer in the field if the race develops any forward momentum.|

runners_data.name: Captain Connor
runners_data.note: Disappointing form string of 48P-78 with zero wins or places in similar-going history, and genuinely a hold-up horse whose natural position is further back than the map places him — the lack of early pace in this race is a material problem for his style.|

runners_data.name: French Diablo
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field and therefore the key pace-shaper; his 1W2P in five similar-going runs and a recent third and win at 22f on good suggest he handles these conditions, and uncontested control over 2m6f is a significant tactical asset.|

runners_data.name: Delgany Second Now
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes the ride for the powerful Dan Skelton yard (T14: 6/23), which is the most compelling angle here; however his form of 5-775 with zero wins or places on similar going is genuinely poor, and he is a true hold-up horse running in a race shape that gives closers little to aim at.|

runners_data.name: Kotgar
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator by nature whose best recent effort was a third at 18f on good ground; sim-going record of 8/11 with two places but no wins tells a consistent story of placing without winning, and with Conor Ring up rather than a leading name, he needs things to fall perfectly.|

runners_data.name: Mc'flo
runners_data.note: Struggling form of -8964P with no wins or places in twelve runs on similar going makes this a very difficult proposition; a true hold-up horse compressed into midfield by the field's shape, and the distance step up to 2m6f has not been tested — the P finish last time out raises jumping questions.|

runners_data.name: Pink Walls
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 60, with a sim-going record of 5/14 featuring no wins and no places; held up naturally but with P0-P84 form including two non-completions, Pink Walls faces a steep task against even this modest novice field.|

races.paceDynamic: French Diablo is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 2m6f novice hurdle and, with no genuine rival willing to press him from the front, he is set to control tempo from the outset on good-to-firm ground at Stratford. With a field composed almost entirely of hold-up horses — Bells Of Ufford, Brionywells, Captain Connor, Delgany Second Now, Kotgar, Mc'flo and Pink Walls all carrying a hold-up or rear-of-field profile — French Diablo will dictate at a pace entirely of his own choosing, likely setting a steady, sustainable gallop that compresses the field and leaves little room for a late sprint to develop naturally. The absence of genuine pace pressure over an extended 2m6f trip on a fast surface plays directly into the hands of a horse that can conserve energy in front and quicken on his own terms, while the true hold-up runners face the compounded problem of having no pace to chase off. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Captain Connor, Delgany Second Now, Kotgar, Mc'flo and Pink Walls are all true closers forced into midfield positions, and Brionywells and Bells Of Ufford are the hold-up horses most likely to organically secure the rearmost berths given their higher ORs and experienced jockeys. This race shape emphatically favours the front-running or prominent profile: horses that can travel close to French Diablo and pounce before the field has time to organise a late challenge hold the clearest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: French Diablo Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If French Diablo bowls along uncontested and sets a pace that suits him throughout the 2m6f trip.
scenarios.body: French Diablo controls every yard of the race, the pace is fair but measured, and he has enough left in reserve to repel any challengers jumping the last; his recent form of P31 at 22f on good ground confirms he handles this trip and going combination.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sitting handy just off French Diablo travels strongly enough to challenge from the second-last and outstay the leader.
scenarios.body: With a pace-compressed race and an honest gallop, a horse lying second or third throughout conserves energy and hits the front fresh; Brionywells has the form (two wins at 23f on good) and the jockey booking to exploit exactly this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and splits the field, creating a gap for a genuinely patient closer to weave through.
scenarios.body: This is a lower-probability shape because so many of the true hold-up horses have been redistributed into midfield and are unlikely to be running from their natural position; if the traffic breaks right, Kotgar's third at 18f on good and Bells Of Ufford's recent placed form on similar going give them the best profiles.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Collapses Field
scenarios.trigger: If French Diablo sets an unusually slow tempo that bunches the entire field turning in, producing a sprint finish that suits a fresh-legged closers.
scenarios.body: A truly falsely-run race could theoretically bring the backmarkers into contention, but with so many redistributed hold-up types unable to secure their natural rearward positions, this scenario is undermined before it begins; Delgany Second Now with Harry Skelton would have the tactical intelligence to exploit it if it emerged, though his uninspiring form string of 5-775 tempers expectations.

watchPoints.text: French Diablo — if he jumps cleanly and bowls into a clear lead at his own pace, he is essentially unchallenged for the entire 2m6f and the race shape revolves entirely around whether the hold-up horses can close a gap that may never be large enough.

Brionywells — watch how Nick Slatter (3lb claimer) positions him in the first mile; if he gets cover just off French Diablo rather than being dropped out last, he becomes the most dangerous horse in the race given his trip and going form.

Harry Skelton on Delgany Second Now — Skelton will look to maximise a compressed pace by positioning handy, which could mean Delgany Second Now races well forward of his natural hold-up style, potentially improving on his modest form string.

Kotgar and Captain Connor — both genuine hold-up types mapped to midfield; if they are forced to race outside their comfort zone chasing French Diablo, any chance they carry is further diminished and they are worth downgrading accordingly.

Going confirmation — the going report consistently shows Good To Firm at Stratford today; any horses with a concern on fast ground should be noted before betting, as the surface will be quick and unforgiving over 2m6f for any horse with soundness questions.

races.name: George & Dragon Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Duke Of Luckley
runners_data.note: An excellent course specialist on good ground (14/15 sim-going, 5W8P) who travels prominently and has strong each-way claims in a field this small; Freddie Keighley's 5lb claim is advantageous at 168lbs, and a return to his winning trip suits him ideally 32 days fresh.

runners_data.name: Seeyouinmydreams
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who will lead unchallenged at a pace entirely of his choosing; good-to-firm ground is right in his wheelhouse (11/15 sim-going) and recent placed form in comparable company confirms he remains competitive, though the 5th last time out is a mild flag.

runners_data.name: Beorma
runners_data.note: Six wins from six recent starts in similar conditions make this the standout form horse in the race; Dan and Harry Skelton are firing at 6/23 over the last 14 days and the 67-day absence is the main question mark — if fit, the hold-up style is ideally suited to chasing down a lone leader.

runners_data.name: In This World
runners_data.note: Firmly the outsider on current form, with a fall, two fifths and an unplaced run across recent starts; the 87-day absence and trainer with no recent winners (0/0 T14) compound concerns, and the hold-up style means this horse needs the pace to collapse entirely to land a blow.

races.paceDynamic: Seeyouinmydreams is the sole confirmed front-runner in this four-runner field and will stride straight to the front from the gates, setting what figures to be a controlled, uncontested pace over 2m1f on good-to-firm ground at Stratford. Duke Of Luckley will press from a prominent position just off the leader's shoulder, but with no rival willing to genuinely attack the pace, Seeyouinmydreams is under zero pressure to quicken early and can dictate precisely how fast this race is run. Beorma and In This World are both hold-up horses who will be forced to settle at the rear of the small field, likely tracking two lengths or more behind the leading pair through the early fences. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader controlling tempo — overwhelmingly favours late-closers who can reel in a potentially slowing leader in the final two fences, provided Seeyouinmydreams hasn't stolen enough of a march to hold on; horses arriving with a sustained run from off the pace are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Seeyouinmydreams Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Seeyouinmydreams sets a measured, uncontested pace and has enough in reserve to repel challengers from the last fence.
scenarios.body: Dictating every yard without pressure, the leader can conserve energy through the early part of the race and then find a second wind when challengers emerge late; the good-to-firm ground suits a horse with a strong flat-track profile in similar conditions (11/15 sim-going, 4W9P).

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Tired Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Seeyouinmydreams' moderate recent form (5th last run) catches up late and the hold-up horses produce a sustained run from the final bend.
scenarios.body: Beorma's exceptional recent record — six consecutive wins, all in similar going — makes it the outstanding closer threat if the pace collapses in the final half-mile; Harry Skelton will time the challenge perfectly knowing the field is small and positional adjustments are easy to make.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Duke Of Luckley Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Seeyouinmydreams weakens sharply from two out and Duke Of Luckley, travelling prominently throughout, hits the front at the last fence.
scenarios.body: Duke Of Luckley's excellent course-and-distance form on good ground (14/15 sim-going, 5W8P) and recent placed efforts give Freddie Keighley a well-handicapped horse travelling within himself in a race run to suit prominent racers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: In This World Lands Gamble
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically and In This World, freshened by 87 days off, produces a career-best from the rear.
scenarios.body: In This World's recent form (F, 5th, 5th) and trainer's 0/0 T14 record offer little confidence, and the long absence adds significant doubt; only a perfectly run race in collapse conditions gives this horse a realistic winning chance.

watchPoints.text: Beorma's unbeaten six-run sequence is the most dangerous form in the race — watch whether Harry Skelton moves early at Stratford's tight turns rather than waiting for the final fence, given the small field size.
Seeyouinmydreams was beaten into 5th on its last run despite favourable going; if that run masked a physical issue or loss of form, the unchallenged lead scenario unravels quickly from two out.

Duke Of Luckley's amateur jockey Freddie Keighley (5lb claim) has ridden this horse before, but in a race of only four runners any jumping error at a key fence could prove decisive — watch the first three fences for jumping accuracy.
In This World returns from 87 days off for a trainer with zero recent winners; monitor in the parade ring for any signs of fitness concern before assessing its viability as a betting proposition.

races.name: Allsopps Love Stratford Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: T Or Coffey
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up horse who returns after 34 days and showed winning ability on similar going (1W at Goodwood Good), but Lewis Stones (3) will need a truly searching pace to deliver a late challenge at Stratford.|

runners_data.name: Borna Gem
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 128 days off for Twiston-Davies, who goes well fresh (1W1P on Good), and her course-distance profile over 16f on Good ground is the most relevant angle — fitness is the only genuine question mark.|

runners_data.name: Zucayan
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type wearing a tongue tie, 33 days since last run, with solid form at 2m on Good ground (1W3P similar going) but his Stratford debut at 12f last time over a shorter trip than this is a slight concern.|

runners_data.name: Getmyfriend
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in this field, trained by Dan Skelton who has strong recent form (6/23 T14), and a winning record on Good going in this distance range — Harry Skelton's tactical intelligence is a significant asset with a clear lead available.|

runners_data.name: Juggernaut
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has placed in ten of fifteen runs on similar going without winning, and the step back down to 2m2½f from recent 26f outings is a significant question; his stamina is proven but his finishing kick is modest.|

runners_data.name: Dream Jet
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by nature, ridden by Nathan Moscrop and trained by Brian Ellison (2/22 T14), who wears a hood and is mapped to midfield here due to the surplus of closers in this field — his true style is compromised in this race shape and that tempers his claims.|

runners_data.name: Mi Sueno
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who ran just 3 days ago, which is an unusually short turnaround for a hurdles horse and must be flagged; has won and placed on Good going over this trip, but the freshness concern under Harry Reed is real.|

runners_data.name: Miss Fedora
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse placed into a midfield role by the race shape rather than by design — Benjamin Macey (5) rides, and her modest OR of 75 combined with a patchy recent record (no completion in two of last five) means her chance is slim even if she could secure her preferred ground-saver position.|

races.paceDynamic: Getmyfriend is the sole confirmed front-runner and, ridden by Harry Skelton, will look to dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground at Stratford — a course where controlling the pace from the front is a well-established advantage. With no genuine rival to press him early, Getmyfriend is likely to stride into a comfortable lead and control the tempo throughout, setting up a race that tests stamina rather than raw speed. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Dream Jet and Miss Fedora are genuine closers pushed into midfield slots, meaning Borna Gem, Juggernaut, and Mi Sueno are the truest representatives of the prominent group. This shape — a single front-runner dictating a fair but uncontested pace — most strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and pounce in the straight, with true hold-up horses disadvantaged by the lack of a truly searching tempo to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Getmyfriend Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Getmyfriend secures the lead unopposed and dictates a measured, uncontested gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Skelton allows Getmyfriend to stride clear in his own rhythm, conserving energy over the 2m2½f trip and arriving at the final flight with reserves intact; horses who can sit just off the pace in prominent positions are best placed to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent tracker times their move perfectly approaching the last and outstays Getmyfriend up the run-in.
scenarios.body: Getmyfriend's controlled fractions mean the race doesn't truly test his stamina, but a fresh prominent horse travelling smoothly just behind could outfinish him on the flat; Borna Gem's fitness after 128 days off is the key variable, while Mi Sueno's very recent run (3 days ago) is a concern.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and a genuine closer can weave a passage in the straight.
scenarios.body: T Or Coffey and Zucayan are the truest hold-up types naturally at the rear, and both have shown ability on similar going, but the uncontested pace makes a strong enough gallop unlikely; this scenario depends on Getmyfriend going faster than expected, which his form profile does not suggest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Getmyfriend sets an unusually slow gallop and the field races in a tight group before a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A bunched finish plays to sharper, lower-weighted horses, but the good-to-firm surface and Skelton's experience make a truly dawdling pace unlikely; Dream Jet and Miss Fedora, displaced from their natural roles, would struggle to benefit even in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Getmyfriend jumping left-handed at Stratford — Harry Skelton's control of the early gallop is the single biggest shape-setter; if he jumps poorly or is pressed early, the entire race map changes.
Mi Sueno ran just 3 days ago — monitor market confidence as a significant drift would suggest connections are managing the horse rather than expecting peak performance.
Borna Gem returns from 128 days off — her price in the market relative to her fresh-horse record is the key angle; if she moves, she can legitimately travel up with the pace throughout.

Dream Jet and Miss Fedora are both true hold-up horses mapped into midfield — in a race with a controlled pace, neither is likely to get the strong gallop needed to deliver their best, and early coverage may be misleading.

Good-to-firm going confirmed across the card at Stratford — all runners are marked OK for the surface, but Zucayan's tongue tie and stepping back up in trip from 12f to 18f is a subtle query worth tracking in-running.

races.name: Thank You To Our Hardworking Groundstaff Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Bobbarelli
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 99 and a confirmed front-runner who goes well fresh (LR 75 days); consistent placed form on good ground (four places from six similar-going runs) suits this surface, but trainer Twiston-Davies yard is 0 from 11 in the last 14 days which is a notable negative angle — headgear (hood/tongue) suggests he needs restraining.

runners_data.name: Youdecide
runners_data.note: Returns after a lengthy 151-day absence for Ben Pauling's yard, which has won 2 from 6 in the last 14 days; a genuine hold-up horse by style, his form of F444P shows both jumping frailty and a tendency to find little, but good-to-firm ground is a positive and the 2m5f trip falls within his distance range.

runners_data.name: Jack Doyen
runners_data.note: Veteran of 10 at a career peak of form — wins at 20f and 21f on good and good-to-soft suit this trip exactly; Ben Case's yard is 1 from 4 in the last 14 days and the prominent style means he gets a good position off the contested lead without burning energy, making him the profile horse for the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Pescatorius
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse who has placed three times in this going band across 6 recorded runs; the 83-day absence is not alarming and James Best is a capable pilot, though the trainer B R Summers has no runners in the last 14 days to gauge current yard form — trips of 24f and 28f in recent runs suggest 2m5f might be on the sharper end.

runners_data.name: Crackerjack Queen
runners_data.note: Good recent form including a second on good ground and active 34-day turnaround for T Ellis (1/3 in last 14 days) are the headline positives; her natural running style is as a true hold-up horse — in a race dominated by two front-runners, she is unlikely to find her preferred berth at the rear, and the 0.93 style-fit flag is a fair caution on her actual effectiveness here.

runners_data.name: Kings Order
runners_data.note: A 5-year-old lightly campaigned chaser who is by nature a hold-up horse; placed once from nine similar-going runs tells a modest story, and while 57 days since last run is manageable, this field's pace structure means he will almost certainly be forced to race off the pace rather than in his preferred tactical position — style-fit of 0.92 signals a meaningful discount.

runners_data.name: Watchoutitscookie
runners_data.note: A consistent prominent racer who has placed four times from 15 similar-going runs without winning; the 37-day turnaround and David Noonan partnership give him a solid tactical base, and if he slots in just behind the two lead horses he could prove a tough nut to crack in a race where the front-runners exhaust each other.

runners_data.name: Fox Wallace
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner, aged 8 and wearing a tongue-tie; form of P-P576 shows recent jumping problems and the horse has never won at beyond 18f which is a stamina concern over 2m5f — 14 runs from 15 on similar going shows he handles the surface, but he is likely to be the lead horse who drops away first rather than the one who lasts home.

races.paceDynamic: Bobbarelli and Fox Wallace are the two confirmed front-runners in this eight-runner field and will immediately contest the lead, creating a genuinely contested pace from the outset over 2m5f on good-to-firm ground at Stratford. Bobbarelli (OR 99) is the classier of the two lead horses and is likely to assert dominance through the early stages, but Fox Wallace has shown a consistent desire to be prominent and will not simply fold away, meaning the gallop should be honest and unrelenting throughout. This contested, end-to-end tempo over a staying trip on fast ground is a shape that classically favours prominent hold-up horses who can track the pace without burning unnecessary energy — Jack Doyen's profile fits this perfectly, while Watchoutitscookie as a secondary prominent type also has a platform. The field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the map can accommodate; Crackerjack Queen and Kings Order are genuine hold-up horses by nature but have been redistributed to midfield on the map, and in this race shape Bobbarelli and Fox Wallace are far more likely to actually secure the early lead positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Bobbarelli and Fox Wallace trade blows from the front and the honest gallop sees the lead horses weaken in the straight, allowing a prominent tracker to pounce.
scenarios.body: Bobbarelli sets a genuine clip with Fox Wallace pressing, burning both leaders out in the final mile of this 2m5f trip on quick ground; a horse travelling just off the pace — Jack Doyen in particular — is ideally positioned to collect when the lead duo cry enough.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Bobbarelli shakes off Fox Wallace early and is allowed to control the fractions, converting class advantage into an uncontested lead.
scenarios.body: Bobbarelli's OR 99 is the highest in the field and with Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell (7) in the saddle on a flat right-handed course, he may find a comfortable rhythm once Fox Wallace fades; his recent consistent placed form in similar going (six runs at good, four placed) shows he stays competitive at this level.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace is truly scorching and the race falls apart in the final half-mile, gifting a late-finishing hold-up horse an opportunity.
scenarios.body: Pescatorius has hit the frame three times in this going band and Youdecide, returning after 151 days, is a genuine hold-up type who could benefit from a strong-run race if fit enough — though the redistribution of Crackerjack Queen and Kings Order means the true hold-up contingent is thinner than the map implies.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers, pull-ups or navigational errors at fences significantly reduce the field and disrupt the expected pace pattern.
scenarios.body: Fox Wallace's form string of P-P576 and Youdecide's recent F444P suggest jumping errors are a real possibility; if the front two falter early through errors rather than fatigue, a mid-pack horse like Watchoutitscookie could inherit an unexpected position and see out the trip on this good-to-firm surface.

watchPoints.text: Fox Wallace's recent record of two pull-ups (P-P) raises a genuine jumping safety concern — monitor him at the early fences, as another exit would immediately change the race shape and remove the pressure on Bobbarelli.
Youdecide returns after 151 days off with a form figure of F (fall) in his most recent completed run — watch him at the first open ditch as jumping errors have already ended his races prematurely.

If Fox Wallace fades or exits before halfway, Bobbarelli could be left completely uncontested in front — a solo leader at this class level on good-to-firm ground over 2m5f becomes a significantly different betting proposition than a hard-pressed front-runner.

Crackerjack Queen and Kings Order are both natural hold-up horses shuffled forward on the pace map — if they are restrained to their true rear positions by the fast early fractions, they will have dramatically more ground to make up than their odds may reflect.

Trainer Nigel and Willy Twiston-Davies are in a 0-from-11 run in the last 14 days — Bobbarelli is their representative here and that yard cold spell is worth factoring into confidence levels around the market leader in pace terms.
